investigator: CIA Office of Inspector General 9/11 Accountability Review Team
employer_controller: Central Intelligence Agency, Office of Inspector General
verification_method: direct visual inspection of preserved official Executive Summary page images; no OCR used
report_or_finding: CIA OIG 9/11 Accountability Review — Hazmi/Mihdhar watchlisting process failure
exact_wording: Basically, there was no coherent, functioning watchlisting program.
scope: OIG assessment of the CIA watchlisting process in the Malaysia-operation/Hazmi-Mihdhar context. The Executive Summary says officers did not timely recommend State Department watchlisting and describes repeated opportunities to recognize and act on travel information.
source_pages: Executive Summary physical p. 9 / Roman p. xiii
Executive Summary physical p. 10 / Roman p. xiv
Executive Summary physical p. 11 / Roman p. xv
records_reviewed: CIA cables and operational/accountability material summarized in the Executive Summary
workpapers_status: The Executive Summary states that roughly 50–60 individuals read one or more relevant Agency cables in early 2000 and describes later missed opportunities; the underlying cables and personnel records are not reproduced in this artifact.
notes: This is an institutional review finding about process and performance. It does not by itself establish intent, foreknowledge of the 9/11 plot, or misconduct by any particular individual.
